title: squalify must publish the library and CLI to nuget.org from a release tag
lead: Adds a tag-triggered GitHub Actions release that tests, packs and publishes `squalor.squalify` and the `squalor.squalify.Cli` tool to nuget.org through trusted publishing (OIDC, no stored API key), and makes the package metadata fit for nuget.org. It does not tag a release.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner decisions (2026-10-27), verbatim: "publish the CLI too, set it up now and tag v0.1.0. 2) yes, set up the workflow, but finish sq-07 and sq-08 before tagging v0.1.0". This reverses the sq-26 decision "publish nowhere".

nuget.org setup by the owner (2026-10-27): user profile `squalor`, organization `SqualorLLC`. Trusted publishing policy owned by `SqualorLLC`: repository owner `squalor-xyz`, repository `squalify`, workflow file `release.yml`, environment `release`, scope "push new packages and package versions", glob `squalor.squalify*`.

prism references squalify as a pinned NuGet package (prism D69), so it needs a published package.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (new), modelled on `DataBall/.github/workflows/release.yml`:
  - Trigger: push of tags `v*`. Fails unless the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`.
  - Build job (ubuntu-latest, `contents: write`): setup-dotnet with `global.json`, restore, build Release, run the tests with `Category!=Corpus` (Package tests included), pack the library and the CLI with `-p:Version=<tag without v>` and `-p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true` into `artifacts/nuget`, create the GitHub release (`softprops/action-gh-release@v2`, generated notes, `.nupkg` and `.snupkg` attached), upload the packages as a workflow artifact.
  - Publish job: `needs` the build job, `environment: release`, `permissions: id-token: write` (and `contents: read`), downloads the artifact, `NuGet/login@v1` with `user: squalor`, then `dotnet nuget push` of the `.nupkg` and `.snupkg` files to `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json` with `--skip-duplicate`, using `steps.login.outputs.NUGET_API_KEY`. Request the key immediately before the push (keys live one hour).
  - Fail the run if the tag version does not parse as a SemVer version.
- `src/squalify.Cli/squalify.Cli.csproj`: `PackageId` `squalor.squalify.Cli`, `PackageReadmeFile` README.md, tags. The tool command stays `squalify`.
- `Directory.Build.props`: `IncludeSymbols` and `SymbolPackageFormat snupkg` for packable projects; `ContinuousIntegrationBuild` only when `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is `true` (local builds keep local paths). Do not change `Deterministic` or the version.
- `README.md`: links that break on nuget.org (relative links into the repo) become absolute `https://github.com/squalor-xyz/squalify/blob/main/...` links; the `../../DataBall/` link becomes `https://github.com/squalor-xyz/DataBall`. Add install lines for both packages (`dotnet add package squalor.squalify`, `dotnet tool install -g squalor.squalify.Cli`) and a stability note: 0.x versions may change the descriptor schema in a minor version until the schema freeze (sq-12).
- `docs/release.md` (new, short): how to cut a release (tag `vX.Y.Z` on main and push the tag), what the workflow does, the trusted publishing policy fields above, and how to add a required reviewer to the `release` environment. AGENTS.md links it.
- `tests/squalify.Cli.Tests/PackageTests.cs`: the CLI tool package is checked under its new ID.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Package_CliToolId_IsPrefixed`: packing the CLI gives `squalor.squalify.Cli.<version>.nupkg` with the tool command `squalify`.
2. `Package_Library_HasSymbolsAndReadme`: packing the library gives a `.snupkg` and a `.nupkg` containing `README.md`, the license expression `Apache-2.0` and the repository URL.
3. `Package_Readme_HasNoRelativeLinks`: README.md has no Markdown link whose target is relative (no scheme and not a `#` anchor).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them fail for the stated reason.
2. Make the csproj, props and README changes.
3. Write `release.yml` and `docs/release.md`. Validate the workflow YAML parses (for example with `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))" <file>`), and run `actionlint` if it is installed.
4. Dry run locally: `dotnet pack` both projects with `-p:Version=0.1.0-local.1 -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true` into the scratch directory, and list the package contents.
5. Mutation check: revert the CLI PackageId, test 1 goes red; add a relative link to README, test 3 goes red.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet format squalify.sln --verify-no-changes`
- The workflow YAML parses; the local dry-run packs succeed.
- `slicer check`

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/sq-29` on branch `sq-29`. No agent commits, no tags, no pushes. The orchestrator commits `sq-29: release workflow` after the gate passes. Tagging `v0.1.0` waits until sq-07 and sq-08 land.
